ideas.truth: Everyone dreams of walking straight out of routine and into an escape, bag still in hand.
ideas.moment: The exact bag you packed for today turns out to be the same one you're carrying as you step onto a Goa beach at sunset — no transition, just arrival.
ideas.key_frame: The bag as-is, now sitting on warm sand with a low orange sun behind it, as if it simply materialised there.

ideas.truth: A well-made bag doesn't need a studio to look good — it looks right anywhere, which is the real proof of quality.
ideas.moment: The same product shot, unedited, now resting on Goa's sand as the sun dips into the sea, its warm light landing on the bag naturally.
ideas.key_frame: Bag centred, low golden backlight, sand/sea/sky behind it, contact shadow falling toward camera in the direction of the setting sun.

ideas.truth: What you carry becomes part of how you remember a trip.
ideas.moment: A blurred figure walks toward the water at dusk, the bag left resting on the sand in sharp focus in the foreground — a memory forming.
ideas.key_frame: Sharp bag in the foreground, soft silhouette walking away into a sunset-lit sea behind it.

why: The customer's request is a pure background swap on an existing product photo — introducing people or narrative motion (ideas 1 and 3) risks changing framing or context beyond 'keep the bag exactly the same'; idea 2 is the most literal, lowest-risk execution of the actual ask.
treatment: One still frame. The bag — unchanged in shape, colour, material and label — now sits exactly where it was framed before, but the flat or studio background is gone, replaced by a Goa beach at sunset: warm orange-pink sky, sun low over the Arabian Sea, sand underfoot. The light on the bag reads as if it's really lit by that low sun — warm, directional, with a soft contact shadow grounding it on the sand. No people, no added props, no text drawn into the image. The whole story is told in one frame: the same product, suddenly somewhere you'd rather be.

decisions.D1_idea: The same bag you already own belongs anywhere — even barefoot on a Goa beach at sunset, with nothing about the product itself changed.
decisions.D2_conflict: A plain/studio product shot feels generic and does nothing to spark desire for travel or a lifestyle; the bag needs a real, aspirational setting to feel wanted rather than just catalogued.
decisions.D3_roles: Hero: the viewer's own imagined trip — not shown on screen, only evoked through setting and light. Brand/product role: the enabler — the same, unchanged bag now placed inside that imagined escape, doing nothing but existing exactly as it always did.
decisions.D4_opening: Bold image, no motion: the bag centred against a full-frame Goa sunset, delivered instantly and completely in frame one.
decisions.D5_brand: Second 0 — the product is the entire frame from the first instant, via the product shot itself; it does not recur elsewhere since this is a single still asset.
decisions.D6_ask_and_end: No spoken ask; any call-to-action is carried by on-screen text added afterward by code, not by the model. Final frame is the product itself, on the beach, per default.
decisions.D7_product_truth: Bag's shape, colours, materials and label — from the customer's reference photo, unchanged. Setting is a Goa beach at sunset — from the customer's instruction, not an existing product fact.
decisions.D8_deviations: 1) Added a contact shadow oriented to match the sunset's light direction — a small departure from literal 'keep everything else the same,' needed so the bag doesn't look pasted onto the sand (per grounding-shadow craft note). 2) Deliberately kept people out of frame despite two idea variants involving them, because the brief explicitly asks to keep the bag exactly the same and a single background-only edit carries the lowest risk of altering the product or its framing.

scenes.prompt: Change only the background to a Goa beach at sunset — warm golden-orange sky, sun low near the horizon over the Arabian Sea, warm directional light raking across the sand from low behind the subject. Keep everything else exactly the same: the bag's shape, colours, material, hardware, stitching, label, and the camera's original framing and angle. Add a soft, believable contact shadow beneath the bag falling toward camera, matching the low sun's direction, so the bag reads as resting on the sand rather than floating. Keep the sand immediately around the bag slightly darker/lower-contrast than the bag itself, and keep the sky and sea lighter and more saturated behind it, so the product stays clearly separated in tone from its surroundings. Keep the frame containing only the bag and the Goa beach setting — no people, text, logos, or other objects. Preserve the bag's proportions and details exactly as photographed.
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: The bag exactly as photographed, now placed on sand with a Goa sunset filling the background — warm orange sky, sun low over the sea, soft grounded shadow beneath the bag.
scenes.s1_feeling: Warm, quiet longing — the calm pull of an imagined escape.
scenes.s2_first_frame: The bag already sitting on the sand with the sunset filling the frame — the idea is fully present in the one frame, nothing needs to develop.
scenes.s3_one_action: None — a single static image, delivered instantly with no motion.
scenes.s4_new_information: The same product now carries a sense of place; the only new information versus the source photo is the setting itself.
scenes.s5_impact: The bold warm colours against the familiar, unchanged bag should read instantly and clearly even at thumbnail size on a phone.

finish.copy_placement: Any tagline or CTA is added afterward as a text overlay in the lower third, kept off the bag and off the horizon line; no text is requested from the model.
finish.end_card: The final (only) frame is the product itself on the beach — no separate end card needed since this is a single still asset.
finish.music: Not applicable — static image asset, no audio bed required.
